clue.text: Nude in act, perhaps

parts.note: the clue pictures a stage show in a nightclub, where a turn might feature a performer wearing nothing

explanation.surface: A suggestive description of a naked performer on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub floor show of songs, dances and risqué turns is the kind of entertainment where a nude act might appear.

clue.text: Temperate part of the world

definitions.meaning: self-restrained, moderate in appetite and desire
one of the great landmasses such as Asia or Africa

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means self-controlled or chaste; as a noun it names one of Earth's major landmasses.

clue.text: Remove the water provided, we hear, for the sheriff's officer

parts.note: to bail a boat is to scoop the water out of it

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is taken by its sound, and the letters written differ

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: Someone bails out water while a sheriff's officer stands by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns IF into IFF, which sounds the same; the whole answer is said like 'bail if'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this officer serves writs and seizes goods on behalf of a sheriff or court.

clue.text: Fragrance from France — the colour at one time overwhelmed it

parts.note: red is a colour

indicators.note: overwhelmed means one word swallows another, so it sits inside the word for 'at one time'

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly
le is French for it, as the clue's 'from France' warns

explanation.surface: A French scent recalls a colour once overpowering something.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost its final word 'it', which the scan shows. 'from France' is the signal that 'it' must be translated into French; 'overwhelmed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolence is a sweet smell or scent, a perfume hanging in the air.

clue.text: A kind face

definitions.meaning: a sort or variety, as in 'not my sort'
a typeface, the design of printed letters

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sort or class, and in printing a typeface, the style of the letters.

clue.text: Child's the one to catch, to relieve mother

parts.note: a child is a baby, with the possessive kept as an S
in the game of tag, the player who chases the others is 'it'

explanation.surface: In a playground chase, a child is the one chasing, giving mum a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the one to catch' is the chaser in tag, called IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after someone's young children for a while gives the parent a break.

clue.text: Shows up a difficulty, with disastrous sequels

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: disastrous says the word sequels is wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Films whose follow-ups flopped reveal a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RUB to BUR; 'disastrous' turns SEQUELS into LESQUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesques are comic variety entertainments, a kind of theatrical performance.

clue.text: Composer providing happiness

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ..., English composer and Master of the King's Music

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was an English composer; the common noun means perfect joy.

clue.text: Warrior, one escorting lords and ladies when going north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the whole run is read upwards
escorting means the first piece walks beside the next, so it stands just before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
lords-and-ladies is a country name for the wild arum plant
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A fighter accompanies a group of aristocrats on a journey north.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords-and-ladies is a British country name for the wild cuckoo-pint. 'going north' turns the whole run upwards, as fits a down clue; 'escorting' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's hereditary military class.

clue.text: Cask Edward put into good order

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A request to Edward to tidy things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument or engine adjusted to work properly has been set right, in good working order.

clue.text: Scot turned round to notice nymph

indicators.note: turned round says the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A Scotsman turns to look at a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the crossword's stock Scotsman; 'turned round' reverses only the name, not the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a water spirit living in a spring or river.

clue.text: Tree being a little distance inside

indicators.note: inside places the small pieces within the word for a being

parts.note: a being is a person
a means one, the Roman numeral I
a millimetre, MM, is a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A tree that is a short way within something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' stands for one, and 'little distance' is a millimetre; 'inside' tucks both into the word for a being.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is a fruit tree of the ebony family bearing orange fruit.

clue.text: Hard water? It depends

parts.note: hard water here is frozen water, and 'depends' is read literally as hangs down

explanation.surface: Asked whether some water is hard, the answer is a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard water' sounds like the chalky kind from a tap, and 'It depends' like a hedge; really it is frozen water that hangs (de-pends) from a ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice is solid water dangling from a gutter or eave.

clue.text: Cut version of 22 ac

indicators.note: version of means a new arrangement of those letters

parts.note: the answer to 22 across

explanation.surface: An edited version of another answer in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges the letters of the 22 across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or book that has been cut has had parts removed by the censor.

clue.text: Ignorant, as I will keep on saying

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll
to iterate is to say or do again and again

explanation.surface: Someone vows to keep repeating that another is ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to read or write, or uneducated in a field, is ignorant of it.

clue.text: Impish fellow fell in river, backwards

indicators.note: fell in says the small piece drops into the middle of the other
backwards says the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Nile is the river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A mischievous chap tumbled into a river and came out backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' makes ELIN from NILE, and 'fell in' drops F inside it. 'Impish fellow' looks like one unit, but the definition is just 'Impish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like a small mischievous sprite, puckish or impish.

clue.text: Sweet beverage with water, frozen

parts.note: liquor is an alcoholic drink
frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: A sweet drink served with iced water.
explanation.definitionFit: A black chewy confection made from a root extract is a type of sweet, or candy.

clue.text: Dungeon — should I be let out for a change?

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a cell asks whether he might be released for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges I, BE, LET and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in its ceiling.

clue.text: The girl we embraced, after I left Miss Maynard in another place

indicators.note: after shows the girl inside we follows the shortened name
left tells us the letter just named departs from the name

parts.note: Elsie Maynard is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard
the letter I is the one removed

indicators.note: embraced means the word we wraps itself around the girl

parts.note: taken as written
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: We hugged the girl once I had parted from Miss Maynard somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: ELSIE less I gives ELSE; WE embracing HER gives WHERE. Elsie Maynard is a singer in the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera The Yeomen of the Guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means somewhere other than here, in a different location.

clue.text: North African fruit

definitions.meaning: a native of Tangier in Morocco

explanation.definitionFit: A Tangerine is someone from Tangier, the Moroccan port, and the citrus fruit is named after that city.

clue.text: It's unclear how such devices explode

definitions.text: It's unclear how such devices explode

indicators.note: explode says the word unclear is blown apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A remark that nobody is sure how atomic bombs go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explode' rearranges UNCLEAR, and the whole clue describes atom bombs, whose working is obscure to most.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic bombs and similar weapons derive their power from fission or fusion of atoms.

clue.text: Is extravagant with music

definitions.meaning: to blue money is old slang for squandering it
a melancholy style of black American song

explanation.definitionFit: The verb, old slang for squander, means spends recklessly; the noun names a genre of African-American song.

clue.text: Most unpleasant fruit is from abroad

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A nasty-looking fruit that is imported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from abroad' says 'is' is translated, here into French EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of ugly, describing something extremely nasty or repulsive.

clue.text: He'll support the queen, after a time

indicators.note: after puts the queen's letters behind the word for time

parts.note: a second is a short time
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A loyal subject will back the monarch after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a loyal subject, but 'He'll support' is someone backing a motion; 'after' sets the queen behind the time.
explanation.definitionFit: At a meeting, the person who formally backs a motion after it is proposed is its supporter.

clue.text: Music, with the French missing the boat

indicators.note: missing tells us those letters are taken away

parts.note: skiffle is a 1950s style of folk music played on homemade instruments
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A musician without his French band misses the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIFFLE, a popular music craze in 1950s Britain, loses LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a small light rowing or sailing vessel.

clue.text: Leading Abyssinian drink

definitions.meaning: the title of the ruler of Ethiopia
a hot drink of wine, sugar and spice

explanation.definitionFit: The title of Ethiopia's emperor; also a hot spiced punch named after Colonel Francis Negus.

clue.text: In front of ship, harmful wave

indicators.note: In placed at the head signals that one word goes inside another

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
ill means harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A dangerous wave strikes in front of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front' reads as one phrase, but 'In' alone is the container signal and 'front of ship' is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great swelling wave of the sea.

clue.text: Dramatist's a washout

indicators.note: out, split off the word washout, signals a scramble of the letters before it

explanation.surface: A verdict that a playwright is a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washout' must be split as 'wash out': 'out' rearranges WASH. George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright of Pygmalion and Saint Joan.

clue.text: In Ophir, aged hieroglyph is deciphered

indicators.note: deciphered means the letters are worked out into another order

explanation.surface: An ancient symbol found in the biblical land of gold is decoded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deciphered' rearranges OPHIR and AGED. Ophir is the gold-rich land of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol that stands for an idea rather than a sound, as in Chinese or Egyptian script.

clue.text: Subject those people to the ultimate in abuse

parts.note: them means those people

indicators.note: ultimate in picks out the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An instruction to put certain people through the worst abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in' takes E, the last letter of 'abuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Anticipate charge for concealing minerals

indicators.note: concealing means one word hides the other inside it

parts.note: a fee is a charge
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Expecting a levy on hidden mineral deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'concealing' says the charge hides the minerals within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to know in advance, to expect before it happens.

clue.text: Wear out the twine

indicators.note: out means worn out, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that something will wear out the string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WEAR and THE. 'twine' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to wind or twist around, entwine.
